subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Ronan Point Collapse and Progressive Failure
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Ronan Point Collapse and Progressive Failure.

hook.text: In 1968, a gas explosion blew out one wall panel on the 18th floor of Ronan Point tower. The entire corner collapsed.

buildup.text: Ronan Point was a precast concrete panel building. Walls and floors leaned on each other like a house of cards.

discovery.text: When one panel failed, the panel above had nothing to stand on. It fell, hitting the one below. Floor after floor.

twist.text: Investigation found joints held together with mortar and gravity alone — no ties, no redundancy, no backup.

climax.text: Building codes worldwide now require progressive collapse resistance. Remove any single element and the building must stand.

punchline.text: One panel fails. Everything above follows. Unless you plan for it.

quiz.question: What design flaw caused the progressive collapse at Ronan Point?
options: The building used wooden beams instead of steel for cost savings
Panels were connected only by mortar and gravity with no structural ties
The foundation settled unevenly causing the entire frame to twist
